title: PlayStation Fans Are Angry: What's Going On?
summary:
Have you ever been really mad at a company? PlayStation fans are right now! Sony, the company that makes PlayStation, said they're going to stop making game discs. That means you might not be able to buy physical games anymore—only digital downloads.

Fans are not happy about this. During a PlayStation event called State of Play, lots of people typed messages like "NO DISC NO BUY" in the live chat. They even used CD emojis to show they want discs to stay.

Some fans are also upset about a game called Destiny 3. They think Sony isn't handling it well. There were lots of comments about that too.

Sony hasn't said anything about the complaints. They usually stay quiet and hope problems go away. But this time, fans are really angry. They want Sony to listen to them.

Why do people care so much about discs? Well, some people like having a physical copy of a game. You can put it on your shelf and even lend it to a friend. With digital games, you might not really own them—just a license to play.

Sony also said in court that people shouldn't think they own their digital games. That made fans even more upset.

Even though Sony had a big event with new games, fans still felt ignored. They want Sony to say something—anything—to show they care.

What do you think? Is it better to have discs or downloads? Maybe Sony will listen if enough people speak up!
why_it_matters: If you ever get a game, it's good to know whether you own it or just have permission to play it, and speaking up together can make companies pay attention.

During online shows like State of Play, PlayStation fans can send live chat messages to react to announcements.

WHAT: Sony said it will stop making game discs, and fans used messages like NO DISC NO BUY to show they want discs to stay.
WHERE: During Sony's State of Play online event, where fans typed their feelings in the live chat.
WHY: Fans are angry because physical games can be owned and lent, while digital games may be only a license to play.
